ss-220559716.blurb: Relationships don't decay. We learn what they were.
ss-220559716.rationale: The most rigorous piece in the corpus: a simulation with numbers and falsifiable predictions, and the decay-vs-selection point is genuinely clarifying. The model itself is never specified, and two predictions and the 'association score' refer to material no longer in the essay.

ss-208463566.blurb: Test a model's values, not its outputs.
ss-208463566.rationale: Clear framing of the oversight gap and a concrete proposal: probe incentive via novel moral dilemmas rather than behavior. No worked example, no engagement with existing scalable-oversight work, and 'degrades more slowly' is asserted rather than argued.

ss-220251918.blurb: AI broke the resume. Trust is what's left.
ss-220251918.rationale: Tight, well-structured, with a clean thesis and practical takeaway. The core idea is costly-signalling theory applied to hiring, and the four new proxies are asserted rather than tested.

ss-209224664.rationale: Useful core/heuristic distinction and a tidy taxonomy that links human moral error to alignment. The failure modes overlap, have no examples, and the alignment link is one paragraph.

ss-208418808.blurb: A letter to Marcus about the minds we're building.
ss-208418808.rationale: The closing letter to Marcus is genuinely moving. The argument before it is rhetorical: 'control is impossible' is asserted, and the human-enhancement turn is a large leap left unexamined.

ss-210543088.blurb: Check the goal before the data.
ss-210543088.rationale: The self-reinforcing wrong-objective loop is a real insight. Repetitive (the list of influences appears twice), abstract with no example, and shares its thesis with On the Wrong Goal.

ss-206772437.rationale: Sharp contrarian thesis that builds to a real conclusion about autonomy. Key steps ('Not might. Will.', bias always compounds) are asserted, and the middle wanders.

ss-215583264.blurb: What a job really buys from you.
ss-215583264.rationale: Practical checklist for evaluating employers. Standard econ (principal-agent, opportunity cost), heavily list-formatted, with a stray typo; more notes than essay.

ss-213921144.blurb: Decide later. Sixteen biases, sixteen fixes.
ss-213921144.rationale: The opening on aimed reasoning is good and well put. The bulk is a catalog of textbook biases with standard fixes; useful as reference, little that is new.

ss-218633709.blurb: Value moves to what's hard to fake.
ss-218633709.rationale: One crisp rule (value moves to what is hard to fake or check), otherwise consensus forecasting plus a YC summary. Garbled sentence near the top, and overlaps The Proxies Are Breaking.

ss-210377028.rationale: The attention-as-obsession idea is interesting. The first third repeats Love, Aurelius nearly verbatim and the core proposal is one speculative paragraph.

ss-207055706.rationale: Real characters and specific detail (the withheld laugh, the thirtieth Tuesday) carry a structure that mostly earns its ending. Held back by authorial interjections ('Morality follows profit') that tell what the scenes already show, and a closing verse with a broken last line.

ss-213722983.blurb: Debts, and a parable about worth.
ss-213722983.rationale: Meditations-style form with a real voice and quotable lines ('then it is jewelry'). Uneven: the Sizoron dialogue swings between earned and grandiose, and the debts list is stronger than the parable.

ss-211829148.blurb: Life isn't short. We waste it.
ss-211829148.rationale: Strong rhetorical rhythm and a good turn toward 'the pull you cannot explain'. Largely Seneca's On the Shortness of Life restated, and it overlaps Scrutinizing the Objective.

ss-220000849.blurb: A self-portrait in the third person.
ss-220000849.rationale: Honest self-portrait; 'a mind that builds beautiful explanations can mistake beauty for truth' is the best line. Reads as prose with line breaks, and much of it needs the reader to know the author.

ss-216230747.rationale: Sincere, with a lovely opening image of the blueberry at peace. The back half dissolves into abstraction and inflation ('majesty so pure', 'immaculateness'), and the ravioli list breaks the tone.

ss-207827995.blurb: Focus × time × the room you're in.
ss-207827995.rationale: Punchy, but the idea is well-trodden and the 'formula' (Focus^Years) is decoration rather than a model. Anecdotes stand in for argument.

ss-221421459.blurb: Sycophancy shows up in the last layers.
ss-221421459.rationale: Only hands-on experiment in the corpus, with a clean neutral/bait design. Twenty prompts, one behavioral flip, logit lens only, no error bars or ablations; the layer-27 circuit claim outruns the data and the piece ends abruptly.

ss-221818985.blurb: A wrong hint, mostly measuring letter bias.
ss-221818985.rationale: A big step up from the earlier sycophancy post: train/test split, paired tests, random-direction control, patching, and an unusually honest section that finds the A-letter confound and withdraws earlier claims. But the headline effect is confounded by that bias, steering was too weak to test anything, and the Substack copy loses the condition and test tables and has typos.

scale: Absolute, not relative to this corpus. 90+ best-in-genre published work (a curated LessWrong classic, a story in a top literary magazine); 80s excellent, would be published in a strong venue; 70s very good with minor flaws; 60s good, clear strengths and clear weaknesses; 50s solid but ordinary or uneven; 40s notes or weak drafts; below 40 not worth featuring. Subscores: 10 is world-class, 5 is competent.
